About the Foundation

A history we must never forget.

Our past is not where the story ends. It is the reason we act—turning memory into education, dignity and opportunity.

How we began

Born from memory. Built for possibility.

The Asaba Memorial Education Foundation was founded by Bienvenu Byamungu with a vision to give hope to young people who had lost hope of accessing secondary education.

Having witnessed the challenges faced by children in underserved communities, he believed that every child deserves an opportunity to learn, develop their potential and build a better future regardless of their background.

AMEF was established in memory of Abwooli Asaba Mary, who passed away on 21 March 2022 after living with diabetes for many years. Her memory continues to inspire the Foundation’s commitment to education, empowerment, health, improved livelihoods and sustainable community development.

Our story is not only about remembering the past. It is about turning remembrance into action.
21March
2022

The reality we faced

For an entire community, secondary school was always somewhere else.

Before AMEF established Asaba Memorial High School, Kiruli Sub-county had never had a secondary school.

01

Distance

Children completing primary school had to travel long distances to continue their education.

02

Cost

Many families could not afford to send their children far from home.

03

Vulnerability

These barriers increased school dropout, particularly among girls and vulnerable children.

04

Lost potential

Poverty, unemployment, child marriage and HIV/AIDS further limited opportunity.

Our purpose

Bring opportunity closer—and make it last.

AMEF works so that geography or background does not decide who gets to learn, develop a skill or build a secure livelihood.

  • Access to quality secondary education
  • Practical skills and entrepreneurship
  • Health, clean water and sanitation
  • Stronger livelihoods for youth and women
